title: Curiosity Credits: Empowering Informed Post-secondary Choices
what_it_is: Curiosity Credits: Empowering Informed Post-secondary Choices

sections.label: Curiosity Credits and CDA expansion
sections.summary: Speaker describes Curiosity Credits, a means-tested way for children to discover interests, and asks about expanding CDA and a SkillsFuture-like scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In my maiden speech, I shared with this House about the idea of Curiosity Credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is a means-tested way for children to draw upon so that they can discover their interests beyond academic pursuit: things like songwriting, sports, robotics and the list goes on.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Since then, I have moved this idea beyond a slogan.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I have filed Parliamentary Questions asking whether our Child Development Account (CDA) can be expanded to support enrichment and exposure beyond preschool settings.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, the response I have gotten is that it is not advisable to open up our CDA funds for enrichment programmes that are outside of preschool.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Well, I also then ask the Ministry of Education (MOE), whether could we have an age-appropriate SkillsFuture-like scheme for students from lower-income households to access subsidised out-of-school opportunities, with proper guardrails.

sections.label: Donor-funded programmes for lower-income children
sections.summary: A donor-funded example through Ray of Hope and Empowering Families Initiative lets children from lower-income families purchase programmes they otherwise could not access.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: One of these examples is through the support from a donor, funded through Ray of Hope and carried out by Empowering Families Initiative, for children from lower-income families where they are able to purchase opportunities to try out programmes that they otherwise would not have accessed.

sections.label: Curiosity Credits 2.0 for secondary students
sections.summary: Curiosity Credits 1.0 gives children opportunities to discover and ignite a spark, while Curiosity Credits 2.0 helps secondary students make informed post-secondary choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: So, to me, Curiosity Credits 1.0 is still about a simple principle – give children the opportunities to discover and ignite a spark.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: But today, I want to build on this idea and focus on Curiosity Credits 2.0 – helping secondary school students to make more informed post-secondary school choices.

sections.label: Mediocre GPA narrows options
sections.summary: A student may graduate from ITE or polytechnic with a GPA of 2.0 or 2.5 out of 4.0 and find options narrowed when switching courses or progressing.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: Perhaps he can still graduate from the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) or polytechnic, with mediocre results, about 2.0 or 2.5 of Grade Point Average (GPA) out of 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: At this point, he wants to switch out, switch to another course or progress to the next level, but with a GPA of 2.0 or 2.5, he may find that his options are narrowed.

sections.label: Motion on better exposure for youths
sections.summary: The Motion's simple point is that youths can be helped to make better decisions through better exposure.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: At the heart of this Motion, it is a simple point.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: We can do better to help our youths to make better decisions through better exposure.

sections.label: Unequal access to exposure opportunities
sections.summary: Internships, job shadowing or informal exposure are more personalised and hands-on but not equally available to all students.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: Some students may get internships or job shadowing or informal exposure before making such choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: These opportunities, they are more personalised and more hands-on, however, it is not equally available to all students.

sections.label: Curiosity Credits wallet from Secondary 1
sections.summary: From Secondary 1 onwards, students would have a Curiosity Credits wallet.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: From Secondary 1 onwards, students would have this thing that I call a Curiosity Credits wallet.

sections.label: Six to eight taster experiences
sections.summary: By Secondary 4, students could have about six to eight structured taster experiences in different clusters to help them decide.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: The target is modest but meaningful – not to expose every student to every possible course, but if by Secondary 4, they can have about six to eight structured taster experiences in different clusters, this might help them to make a better decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: If we do this right, we can help students to enrol into courses with a clearer fit alignment and reduce the risk of course mismatch, disengagement and later pathway regret.

sections.label: Applied learning modules
sections.summary: The speaker says their research calls this applied learning modules.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: From my research, it is what we called applied learning modules.

sections.label: Wallet from Secondary 1
sections.summary: Every child would have a visible Curiosity Credits wallet from Secondary 1, not Secondary 2.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: First, at the student level, every child would have a visible Curiosity Credits wallet from Secondary 1, not Secondary 2.

sections.label: Shorter lower-barrier tasters
sections.summary: The tasters can be shorter and lower-barrier, perhaps three to four hours each.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: Third, at the course level, the tasters can be shorter and lower-barrier, perhaps three to four hours for each.

sections.label: Exposure in protected curriculum time
sections.summary: Such exposure should build into protected curriculum time.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: Fourth, at the system level, such exposure should build into protected curriculum time.

sections.label: Opportunity inequality in Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states that opportunity inequality exists and that systems and structures should seek to reduce this gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: As we progress as a country, opportunity inequality exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: But we should acknowledge this gap and ensure that our systems and structures seek to reduce it.

sections.label: Exposure and fair chance
sections.summary: The passage states it must be built through exposure, reflection and experience, and that more can be done for young Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: It has to be built through exposure, reflection and experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: But I believe we can do more to ensure that every young Singaporean has relevant information, meaningful exposure and a fair chance to make better decisions.

sections.label: MOE three-pronged approach
sections.summary: The passage states MOE has a three-pronged approach to help students discover interests, develop potential and choose post-secondary pathways.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: In fact, what might look like a suitable pathway at 16 may look very different just several years later.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: We must, instead, ready our students with resilience and adaptability towards change through developing their 21st Century Competencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: With this goal in mind, MOE has a three-pronged approach in supporting students to discover their interests and strengths, develop their potential and choose their post-secondary pathways wisely.

sections.label: Polytechnic entry programmes
sections.summary: The passage states polytechnics offer the Polytechnic Foundation Programme and Common Entry Programme, letting students choose a broad cluster.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Our polytechnics offer the Polytechnic Foundation Programme and Common Entry Programme, allowing students to choose a broad cluster, such as the sciences, without deciding on a specific diploma programme when they enter polytechnic.

sections.label: Applied Learning Modules
sections.summary: The passage states polytechnics and ITE offer three-day Applied Learning Modules spanning six broad clusters for hands-on learning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: To support students’ transition from secondary school, polytechnics and ITE offer three-day Applied Learning Modules (ApLMs), as highlighted by Mr David Hoe earlier, providing students with authentic and immersive hands-on learning experiences that help them to discover their interests and their strengths, and make informed education and career choices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Spanning six broad clusters – Business, Engineering, Information Technology, Hospitality and Tourism, Mathematics and Science, Media and Design – each ApLM module exposes students to at least one related IHL course and industry.

sections.label: Support for disadvantaged students
sections.summary: The passage states MOE dedicates additional resources and an Opportunity Fund to support students from disadvantaged backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Third, MOE dedicates additional resources to support and empower students from disadvantaged backgrounds in their exploration of options and opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Since 2019, MOE has provided more resourcing for schools with more students from disadvantaged backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: MOE's Opportunity Fund also provides financial support to enable such students to access development opportunities.

sections.label: MOE Pathfinder Plus programme
sections.summary: MOE's Pathfinder Plus programme lets Secondary 3 and 4 students from disadvantaged backgrounds attend workshops curated according to their strengths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Through MOE's Pathfinder Plus programme, Secondary 3 and 4 students from disadvantaged backgrounds attend workshops that MOE curates according to the students' strengths.
